pairs.why: Both are near-identical flat wall clocks with the same glossy orange rim and face, so neither is clearly closer to the real card's softer red-orange rim.
A hangs flat against the striped wall like the real clock, while B stands on a floor with a ground shadow, which changes how the object is built and staged.
A matches the real card's wall-mounted clock against stripes, while B sits on a floor plane the real card doesn't have.
B is the wall-mounted clock that matches the real card, while A stands on a floor with a cast ground shadow.
A is a solid, believable open wooden coffin in calmer painted browns like the real props, while B is a flat, glossy orange slab that reads more like a sticker.
B's ball has softer, richer inner shading closer to the real cards' painted glass, while A's stark white highlight and plain fill look more like generic clip-art, though it's a close call.
B has rivets, rimmed portholes and a bolted body like the real submarine, so it reads as a built object, while A is a smoother, simpler toy shape.
A's soft, matte teal clay-plastic finish matches the real cards' rubbery toy look, while B's chrome silver body is glossier and more metallic than anything in the set.
